statement.p: Compute the line integral of the vector field \mathbf{F}=\left\lt 3zy^{-1}, 4x,-y\right> over the path \mathbf{c}(t) = (e^t,e^t,t) for -3\le t \le 3

static.solution:
[Step 1.] Calculate the integrand.
We write out the vectors and compute the integrand: \mathbf{c}(t)=\left( e^t , e^t ,t\right) \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)= \left\lt 3z y^{-1},4x,-y \right> = \left\lt 3t e^{-t},4 e^t ,- e^t \right> {\mathbf{c}}'(t)= \left\lt e^t , e^t ,1 \right> The integrand is the dot product: \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\cdot {\mathbf{c}}'(t) = \left\lt 3t e^{-t},4 e^t ,- e^t \right>\cdot \left\lt e^t , e^t ,1 \right>=3t e^{-t}\cdot e^t +4 e^t \cdot e^t - e^t \cdot 1= 3t+4 e^{2t}- e^t [Step 2.] Evaluate the integral.
The vector line integral is: \int_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{F} \cdot \,d\mathbf{\,s} = \int_{-3}^{3} \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\cdot {\mathbf{c}}'(t) \,dt= \int_{-3}^{3} \left(3t+4 e^{2t}- e^t \right) \,dt=0+\int_{-3}^{3} \left(4 e^{2t}- e^t \right) \,dt= 2 e^{2t}- e^t \bigg|_{-3}^{3}= \left(2 e^{6}-e^{3}\right)-\left(2 e^{-6}- e^{-3}\right)= 2\left( e^{6}- e^{-6}\right)-\left(e^{3}- e^{-3}\right)\approx 786.817
